title: Dispatch: a regular constructed language looks like any natural one; if the blue team builds a language, build an a priori one
statement: Esperanto is now pinned (C-052, Zamenhof's Hamleto), and on the practice evaluation layout it sits at the natural-language median on every word-level statistic we register: one-glyph copies of the last ten words 0.021 (manuscript 0.210, natural median 0.025), glyph entropy given two glyphs 2.54 bits (manuscript 1.94, natural median 2.58), edge-glyph dependence 0.125 (manuscript 0.230), singletons 0.674 (manuscript 0.711). So an invented language of Esperanto's kind, words borrowed and inflected, does nothing to explain the manuscript; the only constructed design that could is an a priori one in the manner of Wilkins or Dalgarno, where words are built from category roots plus one-letter modifiers, which would produce one-glyph variants in quantity, and that is the version P-G-006 should try. Esperanto does not yet enter reference comparisons (its calibration share is under 4,000 words); a second Zamenhof text is submitted to fix that. On the attack format, a code change in review adds cut 'book': the attacker writes a whole book and the scorer lays a random draw of its pages, in book order, onto the hidden pages, so long-range facts are no longer met just because text is laid end to end (P-G-007). Until it is merged, long-range facts registered against 'lines'-cut attacks should say so in their source.
check: None: a dispatch. Esperanto values from the practice evaluation layout with the pinned text poured into the selected token slots, as vs/dsl.py does for reference languages; the code change is branch code-P-G-007-fleet-opus.
